# Nigerian bills and airtime through AbaPay

> Experimental listing: an early-stage third-party seller. buy has not reviewed it; confirm with the user before paying.

Sold by [AbaPay](https://www.abapays.com) directly, not through the buy gateway: the
payment goes to AbaPay's wallet and AbaPay pays the biller. Support: support@abapays.com.

| route | price | input |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/pay/x402` | the bill's value plus fees, from about 0.05 USD | JSON body, below |
| `GET /api/pay/x402` | same | the same fields as query parameters |

## This moves real money to a third party

Every call pays a real bill. buy cannot reverse or refund a bill payment: a top-up sent
to the wrong phone number or meter is gone. Before **every** payment, get the user's
explicit confirmation of all three:

- the recipient (`phone`, or `billersCode` for a meter, smartcard or account), read back
  character by character;
- the amount in naira;
- the quoted stablecoin price from `buy_pay_quote`, not only the naira face value.

## The request

| field | required | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `serviceID` | yes | biller code, for example `mtn`, `ikeja-electric`, `dstv` |
| `amount` | yes | face value of the bill in Nigerian naira (NGN) |
| `serviceCategory` | no | `AIRTIME`, `DATA`, `ELECTRICITY`, `CABLE`, `EDUCATION` or `INTERNATIONAL` |
| `phone` | for airtime and data | recipient phone number, also used for the receipt |
| `billersCode` | for electricity, cable | meter number, smartcard number or account id |
| `variation_code` | for data, cable, exam PINs | plan code from AbaPay's catalogue |

```json
{"serviceID":"mtn","serviceCategory":"AIRTIME","amount":1000,"phone":"0803XXXXXXX"}
```

## Buying it

The price depends on the bill, so quote the exact body you will send. An empty request
returns a 0.05 USD placeholder that is not the price of any real bill.

```text
buy_pay_quote
  url:    https://agents.abapays.com/api/pay/x402
  method: POST
  body:   "{\"serviceID\":\"mtn\",\"serviceCategory\":\"AIRTIME\",\"amount\":1000,\"phone\":\"0803XXXXXXX\"}"
```

Then `buy_curl` with the same url, method and body, and `maxAmount` from the quote. The
402 offers USDC, USD₮ and USA₮ on Celo; pass `token` (MCP) or `--token` (CLI) to pay in
USD₮ (`USDT`) or USA₮ (`USAT`). From the CLI:

```sh
buy quote -X POST -H 'content-type: application/json' --data '<body>' https://agents.abapays.com/api/pay/x402
buy curl --max-amount <quoted amount> -X POST -H 'content-type: application/json' --data '<body>' https://agents.abapays.com/api/pay/x402
```

## What comes back

A receipt: `success`, `status`, `message`, AbaPay's `request_id`, `amount_naira`,
`token_used` and the settlement `tx_hash`. For prepaid electricity the response carries the
meter token the user types into the meter. Show it to the user and keep the whole response:
it is the only copy.

## Failures

A response with a payment receipt header was paid for, whatever its status. Never retry a
timeout or a `5xx` on this route automatically: the bill may already have been paid. Run
`buy receipts --resolve`, then ask AbaPay with the `request_id` or transaction hash.

# Argentine FX, inflation, holidays and CUIT/CBU checks

> Experimental listing: an early-stage third-party seller. buy has not reviewed it; confirm with the user before paying.

Sold directly by AR Data Agent, not through the buy gateway: the payment goes to the
seller's wallet. Contact: landingen24h@mail.grokbot.com. Machine-readable route list:
`https://landingen24h.com/celo/`.

| route | what it returns | price | query |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /celo/ar/dolar` | USD/ARS buy and sell quotes per market | 0.01 | `casa`: `all`, `oficial`, `blue`, `mep`, `ccl`, `cripto`, `tarjeta` or `mayorista` |
| `GET /celo/ar/inflacion` | INDEC CPI, monthly and year on year, cumulative between months | 0.01 | `from`, `to` (`YYYY-MM`), `amount` to adjust, all optional |
| `GET /celo/ar/feriados` | national holidays, business-day math | 0.01 | `year` (`YYYY`), `date` (`YYYY-MM-DD`), `add_business_days` (1 to 60, needs `date`) |
| `GET /celo/ar/cuit` | CUIT/CUIL check digit and entity type | 0.01 | `cuit`, required: 11 digits, dashes optional |
| `GET /celo/ar/cbu` | CBU/CVU check digits and bank | 0.01 | `cbu`, required: 22 digits |

Prices are in USDC, USD₮ or USA₮ on Celo. The 402 also offers wARS (Argentine peso
token), which buy does not pay with; buy picks one of the three dollar tokens.

## Buying it

Quote the exact URL, query string included. `/cuit` and `/cbu` answer `400
cuit_required` (or `cbu_required`) with nothing charged until the identifier is in the
query, so quote them with it.

```text
buy_pay_quote
  url:    https://landingen24h.com/celo/ar/dolar?casa=blue
  method: GET
```

Then `buy_curl` with the same url and `maxAmount` from the quote. From the CLI:

```sh
buy quote 'https://landingen24h.com/celo/ar/dolar?casa=blue'
buy curl --max-amount 0.01 'https://landingen24h.com/celo/ar/dolar?casa=blue'
```

A CUIT identifies a person or a company, and a CBU a bank account. Send only identifiers
the user gave you for this check.

## What comes back

`/dolar`: `currency_pair`, `quotes` (one per market with `compra`, `venta`, `spread` and
`updated_at`) and the `source`. Quotes are ARS per 1 USD. `/cuit`: `valid`, `formatted`,
`entity_type` and the expected check digit. `/cbu`: `valid`, `type` (CBU or CVU), the bank
name and whether each block's check digit passes. A validation result says the number is
well formed; it does not say the account or taxpayer exists.

## Failures

A response with a payment receipt header was paid for, whatever its status. Never retry a
timeout automatically: run `buy receipts --resolve` first.

# buy API gateway

Start with a free `GET https://gateway.usebuy.ai/v1/catalog`. It lists the currently
available capabilities, request schemas, token contracts, and indicative prices. Treat
that catalog as the live source for discovery, but quote the exact `POST` body before
paying: the request's 402 challenge is authoritative. Every challenge can be paid with
x402 v1, which is what `buy` uses; the catalog's `payment.protocols` lists any other
protocol the gateway also takes.

The catalog exposes a disposable agent-browser rental plus 170 inspected Monid APIs: 19
for X, 36 for Instagram, 33 for TikTok, 22 for Reddit, 32 for YouTube, 25 for LinkedIn,
and 3 for flights. China Southern is intentionally excluded. The original eight data
routes remain short aliases; the catalog supplies the generated route and input schema
for every additional tool. Callers do not pass upstream credentials.

For generated routes, send the inspected input envelope shown in the catalog, normally
`{"queryParams": {...}}` for direct APIs or `{"body": {...}}` for scraper APIs.
Per-result tools also require an advertised `maxResults` bundle. That bundle is a hard
upstream cap and is not prorated if fewer results are returned.

For an agent, call `buy_pay_quote` with the catalog capability's URL, `method: POST`, and
the exact JSON body as a raw string. Show the user the selected token and amount before
calling `buy_curl` with the same URL, method, and body. Never automatically retry a
timeout or `settle_uncertain`; those responses explicitly report `retryable: false`.
A `settle_uncertain` response carries no result. Keep its `correlationId` and the
payment receipt: `buy receipts` lists it, and `buy receipts --resolve` asks the token
contract whether the payment settled. To recover a result you paid for, open an issue at
https://github.com/celo-org/buy-skill/issues with the correlation ID and the settlement
transaction, and do not pay again.

For a browser rental, quote and buy `POST /v1/browser/sessions` with a
`durationMinutes` of 1, 2, 3, 5, or 10. Save the `browser.accessToken` from the paid
response and send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` to the returned `statusUrl` and
`commandUrl`. Supported command actions are `open`, `snapshot`, `click`, `check`,
`uncheck`, `focus`, `hover`, `fill`, `type`, `press`, `scroll`, `wait`, `get`, `back`,
`forward`, `reload`, and `screenshot`. Close early with `DELETE statusUrl`; the fixed
rental price is not prorated.

CLI users can fetch the free catalog with ordinary curl, obtain a 402 quote with an
unpaid POST, then make the approved purchase with `buy curl --max-amount <token amount>`.
The CLI cap is in whole token units; MCP's `maxAmount` is in atomic six-decimal units.

Every 402 for a `/v1/*` capability also lists one `celo-sepolia` USDC offer at the same price:
the sandbox (the partner routes under `/chainstack` and `/cencori` are mainnet only). It is
USDC only (no USDT or USAT on Celo Sepolia). `buy --sandbox curl` or `buy_curl` with
`sandbox: true` pays it with test USDC from an account named `sandbox` that the CLI creates
on first use; `POST https://gateway.usebuy.ai/v1/sandbox/fund {"address": "0x…"}` hands
out 1 test USDC per address per UTC day, and the CLI calls it on its own when that account
is short. The upstream call is real, so the gateway caps sandbox upstream cost at 2 USD per
day in total and 0.10 USD per payer per day and answers 429 past either. Test USDC has no
value; the sandbox is for trying a capability, not for production traffic.

The same host also proxies the SQD Portal for free, with no 402 and a per-IP rate limit:
blockchain data across 100+ chains for indexers. `GET https://gateway.usebuy.ai/sqd/datasets`
lists the datasets; per dataset there are `head`, `finalized-head`, `metadata` and
`timestamps/<unix seconds>/block` (GET) and `stream` / `finalized-stream` (POST a SQD
query). The catalog lists these routes under `freeServices`. The limit is 120 requests a
minute per IP with a burst of 20; every `/sqd` response carries `RateLimit-Limit` (the
burst, 20), `RateLimit-Policy` (`120;w=60`), `RateLimit-Remaining` and `RateLimit-Reset`
(seconds until the burst is back), and a 429 adds `Retry-After`.
Default download limits: 512 MiB (536,870,912 bytes) per response, 5 minutes total,
15 seconds for upstream headers and 30 seconds of upstream idle time. Deployments can
override these limits. Bodies stream with backpressure; upstream idle
timing pauses while a slow client blocks writes, but the total deadline keeps running.
A limit or upstream failure after headers closes the connection; resume from the last
complete block. Before headers, timeouts return 504 and byte-limit failures return 502.
Every stream line carries
`header.number` (the gateway adds `fields.block.number` to the query if it is missing), so
an indexer that loses the connection resumes with `fromBlock` set to the last line's block.

# Disposable Linux VM (x402 only)

The public buy gateway sells a real, short-lived Debian VM that runs one script as root
and returns its output. `POST <service_url>` with `{"script": "…", "machineType": "e2-micro"}`
returns `402 Payment Required` with an x402 envelope priced for that exact body; paying
the challenge provisions the VM and returns a signed poll URL for the result.

Before choosing a size, free `GET https://usebuy.ai/google/catalog`. Compare
each `machineTypes` entry's `machineType`, `priceAtomic`, `memoryGb`, `vcpu` (guaranteed CPU share),
and `attestationRequired` to choose the cheapest size that meets the workload's needs
and the payer's attestation availability. Compare `priceAtomic` numerically (it is a
six-decimal atomic amount encoded as a string). Read `responseWait` before paying: the paid
request can take several minutes; do not interrupt it after payment settles.

For agents: quote first with `buy_pay_quote`. Then pay through `buy_curl` with `maxAmount`
set to the MCP quote's `price.atomic` (`maxAmountRequired` in the raw 402 response)
— atomic units, six decimals — or through the CLI
with `buy curl --max-amount <decimal>`, where the cap is in whole tokens (`0.02` is two
cents). The two interfaces do not share units. The 402 is intercepted, an EIP-3009
`TransferWithAuthorization` is signed locally, and the retried response settles on Celo
mainnet. Payment is irreversible. The `e2-standard-*` sizes additionally require a Self.xyz
attestation; see `buy/demo-quotes-kyc`. The quote, not the catalog, is authoritative for
the exact request's price and requirements; keep the URL, method, headers and body
unchanged between quote and payment.

After purchase, free `GET` the exact returned `poll` URL about every 15 seconds; do not
reconstruct it from the transaction or instance name. There is no top-level `status`:

- Missing or null `scriptStatus`: the script is pending; continue polling while the lease is live.
- `scriptStatus: "done"`: return `result` to the user and stop.
- `scriptStatus: "failed:<code>"`: return the captured `result` and exit code, then stop.
- `scriptStatus: "not_requested"`: an SSH lease has no submitted script and will never reach `done`; return its connection details.
- `vmStatus: "DELETED"` or `"PREEMPTED"`, HTTP 404 (`no such lease`), or a passed `expiresAt`: stop; report any retained result, otherwise explain that the lease ended without a collected result. Do not automatically buy again.

The optional `order-compute` skill provides additional CLI and SSH guidance.

# LLM inference through Cencori

OpenAI-compatible chat completions. Cencori routes the request to the upstream model and
injects its own credential; the caller never holds an API key.

| route | price | body |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /cencori/v1/chat/completions` | 0.01 USDC | OpenAI chat-completions shape |

## Closed beta: one model

Only `maximo-atlas-1.3` is served. The gateway reads the body before quoting: any other
`model`, a missing one, or a body that is not a JSON object is refused with `400` and
costs nothing. Larger models arrive once the commercial terms are settled.

Include a non-empty `messages` array and set `max_tokens` to **256, 1024 or 4096**.
The body may contain only `model`, `messages`, `max_tokens`, `temperature`, `top_p`,
`stop` and `seed`. Streaming, tools, alternate output-limit fields and multiple
completions are refused before payment. The request body limit is 32 KiB; do not
append a query string to this endpoint.

Text only. Each message carries only `role`, `content` and an optional `name`. Its
`content` is a string, or an array of `{"type": "text", "text": "..."}` parts. Image,
audio and file parts are refused before payment.

Of the body, that is all the gateway checks before quoting: which fields are present,
the values of `model` and `max_tokens`, and that every message is text. It does not
check roles, order or any other value. A request with no `messages`, or an empty array,
is quoted and charged like any other, and what Cencori makes of it arrives after
payment.

```json
{
  "model": "maximo-atlas-1.3",
  "max_tokens": 256,
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Summarise this in one line: ..."}]
}
```

## Flat price per completion

One call, one price, whatever the response length. The price does not vary with tokens,
so there is nothing to reconcile afterwards. Choose one of the three supported output
limits with `max_tokens`; that choice does not change what you pay.

This is deliberate. x402 settles the amount signed into the EIP-3009 authorisation, so a
"pay up to X, settle actual usage" flow is not expressible today (see `cpay#21`). A flat
price is honest about that rather than implying metering that does not happen.

The gateway bounds the request size and output limit before quoting. Its upstream
allowance, when configured, retains a conservative per-call reserve; provider credit
and project spending limits are maintained by the operator.

## Buying it

```text
buy_pay_quote
  url:    https://gateway.usebuy.ai/cencori/v1/chat/completions
  method: POST
  headers: {"content-type":"application/json"}
  body:   "{\"model\":\"maximo-atlas-1.3\",\"max_tokens\":256,\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"hi\"}]}"
```

Then `buy_curl` with the same url, method and body, and `maxAmount` from the quote.

## What comes back

The upstream OpenAI-compatible response: `choices[0].message.content`, plus `usage` with
prompt, completion and total tokens. Report the content to the user; `usage` is
informational only and does not affect the price paid.

## Failures

Refused before payment, so they cost nothing and carry no `X-PAYMENT-RESPONSE`:

- `400` for a field outside the list above, a missing or unsupported `model` or
  `max_tokens`, a query string, a body that is not a JSON object, or a message
  that is not text (an image, audio or file part, or a key other than `role`,
  `content` and `name`).
- `405` for a paid request with any method but `POST`, `413` for a body over 32 KiB. An
  unpaid request with no body, by `POST`, `GET` or `HEAD`, gets the `402` with the price.
- `429` from the gateway's own rate limit. Wait for `Retry-After`, then retry.
- `503` with `paymentSettled: false` when the upstream allowance is spent.

A failure after settlement was paid for, and carries an `X-PAYMENT-RESPONSE` receipt:

- any status Cencori itself returns, its own `400`, `429` or `5xx` included;
- `504` from the gateway when Cencori has not finished within 180 seconds, and `502`
  when its response could not be relayed.

That header, not the status, says whether a call was charged (a payment made with another
protocol the catalog lists gets its receipt under that protocol's own header). Check for it before
retrying a failure: if it is there, a retry signs a new authorisation and is charged
again. When the response was lost or is a `500`, run `buy receipts --resolve` before
doing anything else.

Some of those paid failures are refunded. When a call settled and you got no
completion, because of the gateway's `504` or `502`, a Cencori `5xx`, or a Cencori
`401`, `402`, `403` or `429` (the gateway's own credential or credit failing, not your
request), the gateway records a refund owed to the paying address, keyed by the
settlement transaction in the receipt. An operator sends it back in the same token
and amount. You do not need to ask, and a retry is charged on its own. A Cencori `400`
or other `4xx` comes from the request and is not refunded, and neither is a call you
abandoned before it answered. Keep the receipt's transaction hash; it identifies the
refund.

# Celo RPC through Chainstack

A single JSON-RPC endpoint for Celo mainnet, served from Chainstack's global nodes. The
upstream credential is injected by the gateway and never reaches the caller.

| route | price | body |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /chainstack/celo` | 0.01 USDC | a JSON-RPC request, or a batch array of up to 2000 |

## Pay per batch, not per call

One settlement on Celo costs more in gas than several hundred RPC calls cost to serve, so
this endpoint is priced per *request body*, not per RPC call. Send a JSON-RPC batch and
pay once:

```json
[
  {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"eth_blockNumber","params":[]},
  {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"eth_getBalance","params":["0x…","latest"]}
]
```

A single (non-array) request is accepted and costs the same 0.01 USDC, so batch whatever
you can. The gateway counts every batch entry, including notifications without an `id`,
and caps the batch at 2000 calls. It also caps body size at 128 KiB. A larger batch,
a larger body, or one that is not JSON is refused before any payment. Fewer calls with
large parameters reach the byte cap sooner.

Every method costs the same, including `debug_*` and `trace_*`. The method travels inside
the body and the gateway prices by path, so it cannot tell them apart.

Chainstack's on-chain reputation counts only ordinary node work. That means a batch of
up to 100 calls, no `debug_*`, `trace_*`, `eth_simulateV1` or `eth_getFilterLogs`, and
`eth_getLogs` by `blockHash` or over at most 10,000 explicit blocks in the whole request,
and at most 10 `eth_call`, `eth_estimateGas` or `eth_createAccessList` calls.
A heavier request is served and
refunded on failure like any other, but it is not scored for or against the provider.

## Buying it

Quote first. The 402 challenge is authoritative, and the price does not depend on which
methods are in the batch.

```text
buy_pay_quote
  url:    https://gateway.usebuy.ai/chainstack/celo
  method: POST
  body:   "[{\"jsonrpc\":\"2.0\",\"id\":1,\"method\":\"eth_blockNumber\",\"params\":[]}]"
```

Then `buy_curl` with the same url, method and body, and `maxAmount` from the quote. From
the CLI, an unpaid `curl` POST returns the 402; `buy curl --max-amount 0.01` performs the
paid retry.

## What comes back

The upstream JSON-RPC response, unmodified: a single object for a single request, an array
for a batch. Match batch results to requests by `id`. A JSON-RPC level error (bad params, unknown
method) arrives as a normal `200` with an `error` member per entry, and is **not**
refunded; the batch was served.

## Failures

Refused before payment, so they cost nothing and carry no `X-PAYMENT-RESPONSE`:

- `400` for a body that is not JSON or a batch over 2000 calls, `413` for a body over
  128 KiB, `405` for a paid request with any method but `POST`. An unpaid request with
  no body, by `POST`, `GET` or `HEAD`, gets the `402` with the price.
- `429` from the gateway's own rate limit. Wait for `Retry-After`, then retry.
- `503` with `paymentSettled: false` when the upstream allowance is spent.

Everything else arrives after settlement and was paid for. Any status Chainstack itself
returns, its own `429` or `5xx` included, comes back with an `X-PAYMENT-RESPONSE`
receipt, and so does a JSON-RPC error inside a `200`. Check for that header before
retrying a failure: if it is there the batch was charged, and a retry signs a new
authorisation and is charged again. When the response was lost or is a `500`, run
`buy receipts --resolve` before doing anything else. A payment made with another protocol
the gateway's catalog lists gets its receipt under that protocol's own header.

## Query parameters

`listings`, `posts` and `catalog` take `q` (free text over names, titles, bios, hashtags

`posts` takes `sort` (`newest` or `views`). `creator/<id>` takes an id from any of the other

query string included, and pay that. The same route with a different `q` or `limit` is a

Ask for what you need with `limit`. A request with no parameters uses the default limit of

A list (`creators`, `posts` or `tracks`) and a `page` block with `total`, `returned`,

A response with a payment receipt header was paid for, whatever its status. Never retry a
